admin.backup_note: One ZIP holding every table as a CSV, plus a manifest of row counts. It is a DATA backup, not a pg_dump: no schema, no sequences, no roles — restoring means starting a fresh platform and loading the CSVs. gov.find.indirect_note: Routes that hand their check to a helper in the same module are counted as guarded and excluded here:
gov.find.k_star_only: Held only by an all-permissions account
gov.find.open_note: Every registered route that carries no permission guard in its own source. Some are legitimately public (sign-in, health, static assets); the ones that are not are the most serious finding on this page.
gov.find.scan_note: Static scan of the source of every registered route, looking for the permission decorator and the in-handler guards. A permission enforced only inside a service the route calls therefore appears here — that is deliberate: enforcement an auditor cannot see on the route is enforcement they cannot sign off.
gov.find.single_roles: Roles with a single holder (continuity risk)

gov.find.uncheckable: This check could not be run — the result below is NOT an all-clear.
gov.find.unheld: Permissions granted by a role but held by no active user
gov.find.unsignable: Approval rungs no active user can sign
gov.find.unsignable_note: A request that reaches one of these rungs waits for a signature nobody holds the role to give. Nothing reports an error — it simply stops until a platform administrator signs it by override. Assign the role to a person in Admin → Users, or point the stage at a staffed role in Procurement → Settings.

gov.raci.exceptions: Where the naming convention does not hold
gov.raci.exceptions_sub: These permission names do not end in _view, _manage, _approve or _admin. Each one is either mapped by an explicit exception recorded in the code, or left unclassified. Nothing here is inferred silently.
gov.raci.sub: Derived from the permission names themselves (_view / _manage / _approve / _admin), never from a hand-maintained list, so this cannot drift away from the code. Permissions whose name does not follow the convention are listed separately below instead of being guessed.
gov.rules.escalation_sub: When the requester is the only person who may sign a rung, that rung would wait for a signature that can never legally arrive. It is escalated one level up the org chart instead. A role with no superior configured means nobody above it, and the request is refused at submit rather than left to rot.
gov.rules.holders: Who holds each role right now
gov.rules.holders_sub: A role with no holder is a governance hole; a role with one holder is a continuity risk.
gov.rules.name: Rule
gov.rules.rfq_quotes: quotes from distinct vendors at or above
gov.rules.rfq_waiver: unless Purchasing records a single-source justification.
gov.rules.sod_dual: Dual role: one person may not sign two different stages of the same request, not even when a delegation makes them eligible for both.
gov.rules.sod_self: Self-approval: the person who raised a purchase request may never sign any of its approval stages — raising it is already their signature.
gov.rules.sod_strict: Strict mode: administrators are bound by both independence rules exactly like everyone else.
gov.rules.sod_warn: While "admins exempt" is on, super_admin and every role holding Procurement admin bypass BOTH rules and can walk a request through the whole ladder alone. This materially weakens segregation of duties. Turn it off in Procurement settings for strict mode.
gov.sub: Who can do what on this platform, which rules the modules enforce, and where the authorisation model has holes. Read-only — nothing on these pages changes a permission.

m_import_missing_cols: That file is missing a required column. The importer matches your file's own header names, so add the missing column and upload again. Missing, then the headers found:
m_import_no_header: No sheet in that file had a Display Name / Alias / Primary SMTP Address header in its first 6 rows, so no users were created. Fix the header row and upload again. Columns found:

ppl.inc.formula: Earned minutes = pieces × SMV. Efficiency = earned ÷ worked. Incentive = (earned − threshold minutes) × rate, never below zero.

ppl.leave.rule: Unpaid leave carries no entitlement and is not balance-checked.
ppl.leave.sub: A request can never exceed the remaining balance, and approving deducts it exactly once.

prob.critdesc.attendance: How many times were they absent without permission or late for attendance/work start?
prob.critdesc.cooperation: Do they help colleagues and act to keep the line's workflow going without disruption?
prob.critdesc.learning_speed: Did they grasp instructions quickly and master the machine/main work tool in the expected time?
prob.critdesc.productivity: Did the worker reach the assigned daily/weekly quantity after the training period?
prob.critdesc.resource_efficiency: Does the worker waste materials (fabric, thread)? Do they keep the machine/tools clean to avoid breakdowns?
prob.critdesc.responsiveness: Do they calmly accept supervisor instructions to change work method/tasks and execute them accurately?
prob.critdesc.safety_hygiene: Do they wear PPE? Is their area organized and clean to reduce accidents?
prob.critdesc.work_quality: How many defective pieces were returned from QC to this worker for rework? (fewer is better)

proc.act.approve_why: DOAM Table 5 A — final authority to commit at this value tier.
proc.act.endorse_why: DOAM Table 5 E — senior support, one level above the tier that took the decision.
proc.act.prepare_why: DOAM Table 5 P — the requester initiates the activity; submitting the request is their signature.
proc.act.review_why: DOAM Table 5 R — verified accuracy, budget and policy compliance before approval.
proc.add_dept_hint: Created with the default approval route — then tune it above.
proc.adv_hint: Paying before the supplier invoices is an advance. Up to 25% of the PO the Financial Director authorises; above that the CFO or the Managing Director, plus a bank guarantee when the order exceeds 500,000 EGP.
proc.ai_draft_hint: Garamento fills the form from plain words — review, then price with 🔎.
proc.ai_draft_hint_req: Garamento fills the form from plain words — review the items, then submit.
proc.all_sub: Every request and where it stands in its approval cycle.
proc.analytics_sub: Where the money goes, how fast approvals move, and where they get stuck.
proc.attach_hint: Quotations, specs or drawings — PDF, image, Excel or CSV, up to 3 MB each.
proc.bcase_ph: The need, the options considered, the return, and the consequence of not proceeding.
proc.budgeted_why: Within the department's approved budget for this period — routed on the §4.1 budgeted ladder.
proc.budgets_sub: Annual budgets and how much each department has committed so far.
proc.builtin_note: Built-in department: it can’t be renamed or deleted — “Reset” clears any custom route so it uses the default rules again.
proc.cov_blind: Some lines carry no stock record, so their requirement could not be netted — they are reported, not assumed covered.
proc.cov_why: Procurement quantity is capped at the net requirement after inventory netting (§3.4).
proc.custom_note: Custom department: removing it deletes its custom route and takes it off the list.
proc.deleg_sub: Let someone approve on another person's behalf while they're away.
proc.dev_blind: Some lines have no target price or stock ceiling on file, so they could not be graded.
proc.draft_hint: This request is a draft — submit it to start the approval cycle.
proc.ejr.none: No approved report exists yet — raise one
proc.ejr.why: Spares, maintenance and workshop requests need an Engineering Head signature before Procurement accepts them, at any value.
proc.export.title: Exports
proc.fc_hint: Buying ahead of a confirmed client order? Cite an agreed forecast instead of a sales order (DOAM §3.4). Only forecasts the Supply Chain Director has agreed, and that are still in date, are listed. Fill in one or the other, not both.
proc.fc_hint_agree: A draft forecast buys nothing. Table 4 L2 of the DOAM puts operational and inventory replenishment with the Supply Chain Director, so only the Supply Chain Director (or a Procurement admin) can agree one.
proc.fc_hint_dates: Leave the dates blank and the forecast runs from today for 90 days — one production quarter. It stops satisfying the gate the day it ends.
proc.fc_none: No forecasts recorded yet. Until one is recorded and agreed, direct production material must name a client sales order.
proc.fc_sub: DOAM §3.4 lets direct production material be bought against a valid client sales order OR an agreed forecast. This is the forecast register: a forecast only counts once the Supply Chain Director has agreed it, and only while it is in date.
proc.fx.routing_hint: approval thresholds route on this EGP value, not the foreign figure.
proc.fx.title: Foreign currency
proc.kind_capex: Capital (CAPEX) — machinery, vehicles, buildings, IT assets
proc.kind_hint: Capital purchases follow the DOAM capital authority ladder — every level signs, and the Managing Director signs above 250,000 EGP.
proc.l2.plant: DOAM Table 4: the Plant Director owns production and maintenance commitments, so he is the only L2 signature on this request. The Supply Chain Director does not sign it.
proc.l2.supply_chain: DOAM Table 4: the Supply Chain Director owns operational and inventory replenishment, so he is the only L2 signature on this request. The Plant Director does not sign it.
proc.memo_ph: Why this order departs from plan, and why it should still be placed.
proc.new_sub: Fill the request — the approval ladder is chosen automatically from the total.
proc.no_quotes2: Add competing quotes to compare vendors.
proc.no_sig: You haven't set a digital signature yet — approving will still record your name, but no signature image will be stamped.
proc.over_hint: Anything above the ordered quantity is held in quarantine, not added to stock.
proc.po.per_vendor: This request buys from several suppliers, so it issues one purchase order per supplier — each document carries only that supplier's own lines, totals and number.
proc.po.rev_hint: This order has been revised — the PO PDF carries the revision number, and every revision (with its reason and a snapshot of the lines) is kept on file.
proc.po.title: Purchase Order
proc.pricing_gate_hint: This request carries no commercial value yet. Enter the unit prices — the value-based Finance / CFO / CEO approvals are added automatically from the total.
proc.pricing_pending: Pricing pending — Purchasing will add the commercial value.
proc.quar.note: Quarantined quantities are not in stock and are not payable.
proc.quar.title: Over-delivery quarantine
proc.queue_empty: Nothing is waiting on you right now. 🎉
proc.reject_hint: A rejected quantity is not received, does not enter stock, and goes back to the supplier under a debit note that reduces what is payable.
proc.requester_no_price: Just tell us what you need — item, quantity and any spec. Pricing is added later by Purchasing; you don't enter any cost.
proc.resp_note: The requester always signs by submitting. Tick the approvers this department needs and set the amount each one applies from (0 = always). Clearing every tick makes this department fall back to the default rules.
proc.resp_sub: Define, per department, who approves a purchase request and above what amount. A department with no matrix uses the default rules.
proc.resubmit_hint: Address the feedback and resubmit — it restarts the approval cycle from the top.
proc.ret_due: Retention expired — disposal may be authorised
proc.rfq.hint: One document per supplier, carrying the same items and quantities as this request with the price columns left empty for the supplier to fill in. Issuing one commits nothing.

proc.route_hint: The route updates automatically as the total changes.
proc.rtv.dues_note: Outstanding dues are the open debit notes raised for goods rejected on receipt and returned — value the supplier still owes back.
proc.rtv.note: Returned quantities were never received and never entered stock. An open debit note is deducted from what this order can be paid, and shows as an outstanding due against the vendor.
proc.rtv.title: Returns to supplier & debit notes
proc.so_hint: Required for any direct material for a client order — fabric, greige, yarn, thread, trims, zippers, buttons, interlining, labels, hangtags, cartons, polybags, chemicals, dyeing, printing, embroidery, wash and subcontract. It must be a real, open sales order: pick it from the list. Maintenance, IT and facility purchases use the cost centre instead.
